title: Whispers from the Liminal — ep. 15 · the city in miniature

nodes.text: WHISPERS FROM THE LIMINAL · ep. 15 · the city in miniature
The city in miniature at Sigsbee’s Deep.
Mark devotes most evenings in the latter half of his life on the micro-sculpture. Most folk jest if he’d have spent as much time keeping up the diner, business would be booming.
Graustark in tiny relief is an oddity curio-tourists have delighted in for years, as its scope has grown beyond even the conventional limits of reality.
“His shape suggests a plastic bag carrying broken bottle dreams, sagged to give. The steady shuff shuff shuffle of dragging feet barely carried along by long since bottomed out heels.

Shoes worn to filament, feet roughened by exposure, heavy weight stagger step, shuffle ball changed. Lurching from a past into the future shiny new. Muscles shred yellowed cotton screwed tight on his frame, tic by tic.

Tatters of the past she left him with, worn with no such pride, an expression of puzzlement, stroke struck and yet impermanent. The derelict dead eyed dreamer, a walking monument to the deal that was dealt him.”
Lane goes shopping at the dollar store for things that break. Lightbulbs, eggs, bottles of spaghetti sauce. Thirty dollars counting sales tax. Four paper bags full.
She pulls up outside his house and lights a cigarette. She shouldn’t, but she is.
A neighbor dog freaks out, yapping through the fence, bounding off at increment heights.
